answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it can vote or claim rewards. A beacon contract records the deposit and releases it only after the account’s activity window closes; identities that coordinate suspiciously can be excluded from payouts, but their deposits remain locked until expiry. This does not prove a personhood, yet it makes a Sybil campaign costly: an attacker must buy and immobilize capital for every identity, including juniper and willow, rather than minting accounts for free.
